newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil civil service reform nears committee vote.
newsitem.headline: Brazil civil service reform nears committee vote.

text.p: A proposed reform of Brazil's civil service may be put to a vote in a committee in the Chamber of Deputies next week, a senior government whip said.

If approved by the committee, the so-called admininstrative reform would then move to the floor of the Chamber of Deputies where, as a constitutional amendment, it requires two three-fifths majorities.

Dep. Jose Anibal, lower house leader of President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's Brazilian Social Democratic Party, said some final touches had yet to be put to the reform, which seeks to reduce the payroll burden of state and municipal governments.

One key point which has to be settled would allow state and municipal governments to dismiss currently unsackable public sector workers to bring their payroll spending to under 60 percent of receipts.

The reform would also establish a 10,800-real (about $10,800) ceiling on total pay and benefits for civil servants, ban the awarding of pay rises by decree and establish measures to reward and punish workers according to their performance.
